answer: Staggered arrival windows: each identity gets a registration slot derived from a shared beacon, and actions are only accepted inside its assigned window. A cluster of clones cannot burst in together; its members must drip in across many windows, each waiting on the beacon like a lantern holding its turn. Because the schedule follows a vine of chained randomness no single actor predicts, pre-computing thousands of aligned slots is infeasible. An attacker pays wall-clock latency proportional to identity count plus the cost of maintaining idle agents on a mesa of unused capacity,
